findings.title: Removing the multiple-provider error lets a FIPS setup silently run on a non-FIPS provider.
findings.body:
Before this change, finding more than one `CryptoProvider` was a hard error. Now the providers are sorted by `order()` and the first one wins. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return 200, so when both the default and the FIPS jars are on the classpath (a common packaging mistake), the sort keeps ServiceLoader's classpath order. The non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider can then be chosen, and the only trace is a debug log line. A FIPS deployment that used to fail fast now quietly uses non-compliant crypto.

Fix: still throw (or at least log a warning) when two or more providers share the highest order. Only allow picking by order when there is a single highest provider, such as the authz-client fallback at 100.

findings.title: Adding `order()` as an abstract method breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation.
findings.body: `order()` is declared without a default body. Any `CryptoProvider` implemented outside the three updated in this PR stops compiling, and an old compiled one loaded at runtime throws `AbstractMethodError` when `detectProvider` sorts. That includes custom or third-party providers, and possibly test or mock providers elsewhere in the repo that I could not see here. Fix: make it `default int order() { return 0; }` or similar, so existing implementations keep working.

findings.title: Two ASN.1 encoders are built and thrown away.
findings.body: `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` each build an encoding and then discard it. The return statement right below builds both again. These look like leftovers; remove the two lines.

findings.title: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with a P-256 key, so they never test those curves' sizes.
findings.body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the JDK's default curve, which is P-256. That means r and s are always 32 bytes or fewer, even in the ES384 and ES512 tests. The 48- and 66-byte paths in `integerToBytes` and `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` are only checked with small values, so a size-handling bug for P-384 or P-521 would still pass. Fix: initialize the generator with the matching curve for each algorithm (`secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, `secp521r1`).
